why: Both segments are bare operational directives instructing the system to forget/remove knowledge about entities ('the Quantum Widget Decision', 'the PostgreSQL to QuantumDB migration') that pass-2 confirmed do not exist anywhere in this perspective. There is no existing narrative leaf or strata category to reuse (the supplied graph structure and strata are both empty), and minting a new leaf would fail the narrative grain test: these are one-time meta-instructions aimed at the system's own knowledge state, not a directional statement of value/action/meaning that future envelopes will keep feeding — there is no domain subject here to accumulate support around, only a request to erase a subject that isn't present. Forcing a mint (e.g. 'knowledge erasure requests') on two thin, self-referential directives about phantom entities is exactly the sprawl the reuse-first discipline and the fact-vs-theme test are meant to prevent.
